result.edited:
People have wearied me. I have grown sick of being a coaching inn where those creatures forever jostle, shout, bustle about and foul the place. Throw open the windows! Air out the dwelling! Toss out the rubbish along with those who make the mess. Let cleanliness and quiet enter the house.

Who will give me the comfort of being alone?

How I used to wait for them at times!

And when that beautiful brother of death came and took me to himself, people lay in wait for me even there. They wove their existence together with mine into a fantastic net, and they tried to pour into my ears and my heart what they themselves were full of… Listen, listen! Do you bring your sufferings here too? Your vileness? My heart can hold no more. It is full to the brim. Give me peace…

So it was at night.

And by day I would shudder when I heard a human shadow behind me, and I listened with loathing to the roaring torrents of human life rushing toward me like wild horses from all the city streets.

The train flew, full of human clamor. It seemed the city was stretching its iron hand out into the field after me and would not let me go. I was irritated by the uncertainty trembling within me: would that hand clench its iron fingers, or would it release me? Could I really tear myself away from this howl and enter the empty green expanses? Would they close behind me, and would the iron hand clatter its bones in vain? And would there be silence all around and within me?

And when all this happened, so simply and imperceptibly, I did not hear the silence: it was drowned out by strangers’ voices, petty, unnecessary words, like chips and straw on spring torrents…

…… one acquaintance, a lady, had had heart trouble for fifteen years… tra-tara-tah… tra-tara-tah… our division was stationed there then… tra-tara-tah… Where are you traveling to?… Tickets, please… tra-tara-tah… tra-tara-tah…

changes.before: would that hand unclench its iron fingers, or would it release me?
changes.after: would that hand clench its iron fingers, or would it release me?
I did not hear the silence
